chapter_theme: A song at Theerthamalai (தீர்த்தமலை): the poet rebukes his own mind, which neither melts at song nor fears the coming of Death, and urges it to cling to Murugan; the praise tells Siva's deeds and Sambandar's ordeals by water and fire.

617.reading: Addressing his own mind, the poet says it does not melt at song, does not melt on hearing, does not melt watching the road by which Death comes, does not desire the release that is the Lord's grace, cannot praise with the tip of the tongue, and will not leave the cage of the body that refuses the good path or see the course of fate written on the leaf; then he says, 'Hear one word: will you not cling to Murugan, who is easy for devotees and removes the two karmas of those who praise him?' The praise names Siva who bent the northern mountain with the serpent for a string, burned the three cities, kicked Death, burned Kama to ash, ruined the sacrifice and set a goat's head on its lord, and Murugan as the guru who sent the palm leaf against the river, showed it unburnt in fire and impaled the angry Jains, at Theerthamalai.
617.nuance: The refrain of negatives (உருகிலை, அறிகிலை, விழைகிலை, விடுகிலை) is spoken to the mind as a separate party, the நெஞ்சு of love poetry turned to devotion. ஏட்டின் விதி, fate written on the leaf, is set beside Death's road. The praise names Sambandar's ordeals at Madurai: சீட்டை எழுதி வை யாற்றில் எதிருற ஓட்டி, அழல் பசை காட்டி, the leaf that swam upstream and did not burn.
